Comparison method

The protocol for measuring Offing against the tools developers already run. It is published before any result exists, so no measure, repository, or configuration can be chosen to fit an outcome. #2173, #2174, and #2175 run it; this page decides in advance what those runs may report.

Published before results: 2026-11-03, written against origin/main at 9d81af78 (Offing 0.7.3). At that commit benchmarks/comparison/ — where the runs write their results — does not exist, and neither does docs/COMPARISON.md. Every number below is read from a file in the repository, named beside it; none is estimated. Where something is not measurable yet this page says so instead of guessing.

1. What this page contains, and what it must not

This page fixes This page never contains
The tools, their versions, and where a version is recorded. Any count of agreements, misses, or wins.
The repositories that are in scope and how a subset is chosen. A result table. Those go to benchmarks/comparison/ and #2177.
The measures, their formulas, and the floors already enforced. A new threshold invented after a run.
Each tool's best configuration, and what cannot be measured. A proxy measurement standing in for a tool that cannot run.

The order is the point. docs/REVIEW.md blocks a merge on overclaimed proof, so this page describes the machinery that exists and says plainly that it is not stronger or more complete than the differential testing already recorded — it extends the same harness to a head-to-head measurement with the fairness rules written down first.

2. The precedent this method follows

Two mechanisms in this repository already separate the rule from the result, and the comparison reuses them rather than inventing a third:

  • The held-out set is "chosen by a rule fixed before scanning and its ground truth was committed before the first scan", and its run "reports its numbers and never fails the build" (benchmarks/held-out.ts, header; benchmarks/held-out-repositories.json: 15 repositories, all selection: "blind", scope of 4 rule families).
  • Blind corpus selection: each of the 557 corpus entries records selection as blind or targeted, and a test fails when one does not (docs/VALIDATION.md). Measured in benchmarks/public-repositories/: 389 blind, 168 targeted.

3. Tools and versions

The comparison runs only tools a maintainer executes outside any scan, as the existing differential harness does; scans stay offline and never execute repository code (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).

Tool Question it answers Runner in this repository Version rule
Offing Which declared or used dependency, runtime, image, or API is ending, and where the built CLI, offline the commit under test; recorded with the run
Renovate Does a newer version exist, and is this npm package deprecated npm run differential:renovate (benchmarks/differential/renovate.ts) pinned and printed per run; the last recorded differential run used 44.164 (docs/validation/differential-testing.md)
xeol (an endoflife.date consumer) Which product version in a lockfile is past end of life npm run differential:xeol (benchmarks/differential/xeol.ts) pinned and printed per run; the last recorded run used 0.10.8 (same file)
Pluto Does Kubernetes still serve this apiVersion npm run differential:pluto (benchmarks/differential/pluto.ts) pinned and printed per run; the last recorded run used 5.24.4 at target k8s=v1.36.0 (same file)
Dependabot Which updates or security advisories GitHub opens for a repository none exists — package.json has no Dependabot runner (measured: grep -n dependabot package.json returns nothing) not measurable at a pinned commit today; see section 7

Renovate, xeol, and Pluto versions are recorded at run time into the result file. This page pins no version for the new runs, because a version chosen now would be a version nobody has checked the availability of; the run records it instead, and a re-run that changes a version says so.

4. Repositories

  • Primary set: the pinned public corpus, benchmarks/public-repositories/ — one JSON file per repository, 557 entries across 20 ecosystem directories. Every entry pins a full commit SHA and carries expected findings; measured: 3,122 expected records, all 3,122 carrying a groundTruthSource (3,080 maintainer-review, 42 migration-commit).
  • Scored separately, never blended: blind and targeted entries are reported as two columns. A result that mixes them is rejected, because the targeted half was chosen for the findings it holds.
  • Held-out set: the 15 repositories of benchmarks/held-out-repositories.json, reported separately from the main corpus, as npm run validate:held-out already does.
  • Continuity set: the repositories that already have committed differential reports, so a new run is comparable with the recorded one — measured file counts: 5 Renovate reports in benchmarks/differential/reports/, 5 xeol reports, 17 Pluto reports.
  • Subset rule, fixed now: a run uses the blind half of the corpus plus every repository in the continuity set. Any other subset must be written here, with its selection rule and a date, before the first command of the run executes.

5. Measures and their formulas

Every measure already has an implementation; the comparison uses it rather than a new definition.

Measure Definition Source of the definition
Finding identity ruleId : path : line — exact, so a near match earns no credit findingKey in benchmarks/thresholds.ts
True positive / false positive / false negative expected-and-reported / reported-and-unexpected / expected-and-missing scoreDetectors in the same file
Precision tp / (tp + fp), 1 when both are zero, to 4 decimals scoreDetectors, same file
Recall tp / (tp + fn) recallViolations, same file
Agreement outcome agree, offing-only, <tool>-only, inconclusive; Pluto adds pluto-deprecated-only the four harnesses in benchmarks/differential/
Not comparable a finding in a family the other tool has no model for notComparable in every committed report
Wall clock the command's own duration per repository, observational the same treatment as docs/BENCHMARKS.md: "a reference point, not a cross-machine performance guarantee"

Existing floors stay in force and are reported, not re-derived: minPrecision 0.95 on all 24 detectors in benchmarks/thresholds.json, enforced where stable is true (11 of 24: 6 at stable, 5 at beta); recall floors beta 0.8 and stable 0.9 (benchmarks/thresholds.ts, recallFloors, decision 0013). The last recorded full corpus run is 2026-11-01 at commit 114f19b: 557 repositories, 3,156 findings reported, precision 1, recall 1 (lastFullRun in benchmarks/thresholds.json). Those findings and the 3,122 expected records above are different counts — one is what Offing reported, one is what the corpus expects — and are never compared to each other as if they were the same measure.

Comparability is a hard gate, not a courtesy. A pair is counted only where both tools can say something about the same dependency in the same file, which is what the Renovate harness restricts to three families (deprecated-package, base-image, github-action). A finding outside that is not comparable and may not be reported as a win, a loss, or a miss. inconclusive — a tool that skipped a lookup — is excluded from both the numerator and the denominator, and the count excluded is published.

6. Each tool gets its best configuration

The fairness rule: no tool is run with a capability disabled that another tool is given, and no tool is given a configuration tuned on a result. What "best" means for each, with the commands taken from docs/validation/differential-testing.md and package.json:

Tool Best configuration, and the command that proves it
Offing the built CLI, offline, on the pinned commit, every built-in detector, cache bypassed, no severity gate, no narrowing: npm run build && node dist/src/cli.js scan <checkout> --no-cache --json. --no-cache and --json are parsed in src/commands/runtime.ts; --only / --exclude exist and are forbidden here because they would remove findings before scoring.
Renovate a read-only token so GitHub Actions lookups resolve instead of returning github-token-required: export RENOVATE_TOKEN=<token> GITHUB_COM_TOKEN=<token> then npx renovate --platform=local --dry-run=lookup --report-type=file --report-path=renovate.json, then npm run differential:renovate -- --renovate renovate.json --repository <checkout> --name owner/repo --out report.json
xeol xeol dir:<checkout> -o json > xeol.json, then npm run differential:xeol -- --xeol xeol.json --repository <checkout> --name owner/repo --out report.json
Pluto run from inside the checkout, with an explicit target version: (cd <checkout> && pluto detect-files -d . -o json -t k8s=v1.36.0 > pluto.json), then npm run differential:pluto -- --pluto pluto.json --repository <checkout> --name owner/repo --out report.json
Dependabot no local command exists. offing dependabot-config . writes a dependabot.yml for a repository to use
(src/commands/dependabot-config.ts); that is Offing's output, not a Dependabot measurement, and must not be scored as one.

The comparison repositories are checked out of the pinned corpus cache, offline, as AGENTS.md prescribes: export OFFING_CORPUS_CACHE=~/.cache/offing-corpus, npm run corpus:warm, then run with --offline; --concurrency stays at its default of 16 (DEFAULT_CORPUS_CONCURRENCY in benchmarks/corpus-harness.ts). Nothing this method adds runs repository code, evaluates a manifest, or touches the network from a scan.

7. What cannot be measured, stated in advance

Declared before the first run, so no run can quietly redefine a limit as a result:

  • Dependabot: it runs inside GitHub's service on a repository's default branch, not against a pinned commit offline. There is no runner in this repository. A head-to-head number for it is therefore not measured; if a run is ever possible, it is on a live repository, and that difference from the pinned-commit method is published in the same table as its result.
  • Runtime and API findings against Renovate and xeol: those tools model no runtime end-of-life or retired-API question, so Offing's largest families are not comparable with them. Recorded as not comparable, never as a win.
  • Update automation in Offing's favour: Offing opens nothing and runs no migration command; the reverse direction (Renovate's automation) is a capability Offing does not have and does not score.
  • Product breadth versus endoflife.date for #2175 is measured against the ground-truth set, and that set's expansion is #2168, open at the time this page was written. Until it lands, the available ground truth is the corpus's 3,122 reviewed records above, and any breadth figure drawn from it must be labelled with that scope.
  • Cross-machine timing: durations are recorded per machine and never compared across machines as a result, matching docs/BENCHMARKS.md.

8. Binding rules for the run and for publishing

  1. This page is amended only by a dated entry that states whether the amendment was made after seeing a result; a measure changed after a run forces a fresh run of both tools, published together.
  2. Both tools run on the same checkout at the same commit, in the same working tree, and the commit is in the result file.
  3. Every disagreement is published as its own row with the evidence link, as docs/differential-report.md already does for Renovate. Aggregate claims without the row table are rejected.
  4. Losses are published with the same detail as wins; the report where the other tool found more is the headline of the run that produced it. #2177 carries that page.
  5. No result changes a registry rule, a threshold, a floor, or an allowlist entry as part of the run (docs/QUALITY.md: an entry may never be added or raised to make something pass).
  6. npm run check gates every run's pull request, and npm run validate:public-repos is not part of it — it needs the network, so a run records how it was executed and whether the cache was warm.

9. Reproducing the tables, and the method

One command rebuilds every committed comparison table from the committed inputs and compares it with the published known result. It runs from a clean checkout with no network, no repository code, and no clock:

npm ci
npm run comparison:reproduce

The command prints the pinned versions and the headline counts, then checks every generated file and the known result byte for byte. It exits 1 and names each file that differs. Refreshing any input is a maintainer action: collect the raw records per each comparison's README, then rewrite the tables and the known result with the same command:

npm run comparison:reproduce -- --record

The pins that produced the published tables are recorded in benchmarks/comparison/reproduce.json, beside the SHA-256 of every generated file:

Pin Value
Node.js >=22 (engines in package.json)
Renovate 44.164.10, printed per run and recorded in renovateVersions
Dependabot not run, as section 7 states; recorded as dependabot: "not-run"
endoflife.date snapshot retrieved 2026-11-06, recorded with its SHA-256
Offing 0.7.3 at the commit each run recorded in offingCommits

Amended 2026-11-08, after the first results: sections 3 and 7 stand; this amendment adds the reproduction command, the known result, and the pins the finished runs used. The corpus has grown since sections 4 and 5 counted it, so those historical counts are unchanged and the current counts are the ones the known result records. No measure, score, subset, or threshold changed, and no table was re-scored to fit the amendment.

These commands build and score Offing's own half. They exist in package.json; run them from a clean checkout of the commit being measured.

npm ci
npm run build
npm run check                    # the gate CI runs
npm run corpus:warm              # needs OFFING_CORPUS_CACHE and network
npm run validate:public-repos -- --offline
npm run validate:held-out
npm run differential:report      # rebuilds docs/differential-report.md from committed reports

Results of the comparison itself are produced by #2173/#2174/#2175 into benchmarks/comparison/, packaged by #2176, and published with the losses in #2177. #2176 also owns later edits to this page: the one command above reproduces the published tables, and its known result carries the pins.

10. Where the comparison claims are already made

The tool-by-tool pages state what each alternative does better today, and each links its evidence: docs/compare/index.md, Renovate, Dependabot, endoflife.date. They are prose claims about capability, not measurements, and they do not cite this page's method as a result. When the runs land, the measured tables belong to docs/COMPARISON.md and point back here for the method.
